channel.title: FastAIAgent Blog
channel.description: Notes from the harness: replay, guardrails, evaluation, and what it takes to operate agents in production.

item.title: Your Agents Answered Ten Thousand Customers. How Many Has Anyone Read?
item.description: Most teams rely on an LLM judge to grade the rest, and nobody has checked whether the judge is right. When someone asks who reviewed this, a model's score is not an answer.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: Which of Your AI Agents Would Fail an EU AI Act Audit Today?
item.description: Most teams answer that with a document. This answers it with production evidence — two agents failing the audit, captured automatically, every record hash-chained for the auditor.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: Turn every production failure into a regression test
item.description: A customer reports the agent did something wrong. Here is the five-script loop that captures the failing trace, fixes it, and makes sure it never comes back.
item.dc:creator: FastAIFoundry team

item.title: Closing the guardrail audit: three silences and three verdicts
item.description: Release 1.64.0 closes the cross-repo guardrail audit. Each of the six findings was a control reporting a verdict it had not earned.
item.dc:creator: FastAIFoundry team

item.title: Can You Prove That Control Actually Operated?
item.description: The question for CISOs and Compliance Officers is no longer whether you have an AI policy. It is whether you can prove a control was operating when the agent made the decision — with a 60-second demo of evidence bound to live runtime.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: Evidence, not attestation
item.description: An auditor does not want a signed claim that a control exists. They want the record that it ran. Compliance evidence produced by the system rather than asserted about it.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: An outage should report INVALID, never a green build
item.description: Agent CI has a failure mode most test runners do not: the thing under test can be fine while the infrastructure behind it is down. Here is how the eval gate handles it.
item.dc:creator: FastAIFoundry team

item.title: Guardrails Aren't Just About What Goes Into Your Agent
item.description: It's what comes in, what tools it calls, and what goes out. Three rules created on the Control Plane and blocking live — with zero guardrail code in the agent.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: Guardrails That Log Violations After the Fact Are Just Dashboards
item.description: FastAIAgent guardrails block before the provider ever sees the data. Define one in code, or author it once on the Control Plane and every connected agent enforces it.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: Where Should AI Actually Be in the System?
item.description: Use the simplest thing that reliably does the job, and only let the model decide what happens next when you genuinely cannot know the next step until you have seen the last one.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: Five People Are Evaluating Your Agent Platform. One of Them Is You.
item.description: The developer, the operator, the CTO, compliance and finance each judge an agent platform by a different test. Ship for one and you lose the other four.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: Guardrails That Actually Block
item.description: Most guardrails observe and report. A guardrail that cannot stop the action is a log line with good intentions. Policy checked before the agent acts.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: An Agent Framework Is Not an Agent Harness
item.description: A framework helps you build an agent. A harness runs it in production — and the difference is everything you need after the demo works.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: Your Strong Model Still Reads a Balance Sheet Wrong
item.description: A capable model still misreads a financial table. The fix is not a bigger model — it is an eval that finds the failure and a prompt change you can prove worked.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: Give Your Agent Memory It Won't Lie to You
item.description: Your agent references a customer trip that never happened. It came from memory — a fact recalled from someone else's conversation. Memory as one object, with scopes you can see.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: You Wouldn't Ship Code Without Tests. Why Ship an Agent Without Evals?
item.description: Nobody ships a payment service on three manual clicks, yet that is exactly how most agents reach production. Datasets, scorers and a gate that actually blocks.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: Your Agent Shouldn't Decide Alone. Here's How to Keep a Human in Command.
item.description: The hard part of human-in-the-loop isn't letting a human approve. It's letting them approve later — hours or days later, on a different machine — without holding a live process hostage the whole time.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: The Agent Was Right. The Data Was Wrong.
item.description: Perfect reasoning over the wrong document is the most dangerous kind of agent bug — no hallucination, no error, green across every dashboard. To find it you have to look at what the agent actually retrieved.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: I See Everything My Agent Does. In My Own Environment. No Cloud Account.
item.description: Your choices used to be free but heavy, easy but hosted, or self-hosted for an enterprise fee. Nobody offered the fourth option — free, easy and local. One pip install, one command, one SQLite file, nothing leaving your machine.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: Your Agent Needs Transactions, Not Just Tools
item.description: Databases solved this 40 years ago. Every framework gives agents tools to act; none give them transactions to act safely. ACID — atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability — mapped onto action-taking agents.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: The Prompt Changed. The Agent Broke. Nobody Noticed for 3 Days.
item.description: Code changes have PRs, reviews, CI and tests. Prompt changes have someone eyeballing three responses before they deploy. Here is the gate that catches a bad prompt before it ships.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: Every Production Failure Should Become a Test. One Click.
item.description: Finding the bug is an afternoon. Keeping it dead across every future change by every future contributor is the real cost — and that only works if the failure becomes a permanent test case the moment you fix it.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari

item.title: I'm Done Complaining. Here's What I'm Shipping
item.description: Five articles on what's broken in agent infrastructure. This is the one where I stop complaining and ship: FastAIAgent, open source, Apache 2.0, runs locally.
item.dc:creator: Upendra Bhandari
